NutriBev Inc. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NutriBev Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NutriBev Inc.'s Q3 2024 results. Joining me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Growth Officer; and Chris Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on six key areas: gross margin analysis, drivers and trends; volume and price/mix analysis; impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions; organic revenue growth, overall and by region; EPS guidance and key assumptions; and market share trends for major brands.

First, regarding gross margin analysis: drivers and trends—we achieved a consolidated gross margin of 46.8%, up 220 basis points year-over-year, driven by input cost favorability, pricing actions, product mix shifts, and operational efficiencies.

Second, concerning volume and price/mix analysis—organic revenue grew 4.8%, with volume up 1.2% and price/mix adding 3.6%, reflecting resilience across our beverages, snacks, and nutrition segments.

Third, in terms of impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions—we navigated 12% input inflation and logistics challenges through hedging, pricing, and diversification, limiting margin compression.

Fourth, looking at organic revenue growth: overall and by region—we posted 7.2% organic growth globally, with strength in APAC and Europe offsetting softer spots.

Fifth, reviewing EPS guidance and key assumptions—for the full year, we're guiding to $4.85 to $5.05 in adjusted EPS, assuming 4-6% organic revenue growth and 150-200 basis points of gross margin expansion.

Sixth, analyzing market share trends for major brands—our core brands like FreshFizz and VitaSurge gained share across key categories, up 100-200 basis points in several markets.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to provide more detail on our financial results.

Jordan Lee (CFO):
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3 2024. Net sales were $12.4 billion, representing a 5.2% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 46.8%, benefiting from commodity deflation, pricing discipline, and efficiency gains. Operating income was $2.1 billion, and earnings per share were $1.28. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $3.2 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for 4-6% organic net sales growth and adjusted EPS of $4.85 to $5.05.

To give you deeper insight into the six areas Alex highlighted, let me expand on each, starting with our gross margin performance, which continues to be a standout amid sector challenges. Gross margin, net revenue minus cost of goods sold divided by net revenue, reached 46.8% this quarter—up 220 basis points year-over-year and 90 basis points from Q2. This is our sixth straight quarter of expansion, with a trailing four-quarter average of 45.5%, exceeding our 44-46% long-term target and outperforming peers like PepsiCo and Mondelez, whose margins sit in the low- to mid-40s.

Key drivers included input cost favorability, contributing 140 basis points year-over-year. Core commodities deflated after 2023 peaks: corn for our CrunchBar snacks dropped 15% quarter-over-quarter to $4.50 per bushel on strong U.S. harvests and easing weather patterns; dairy for PlantPower shakes and ready-to-drink beverages fell 8% with normalized EU and U.S. production. Cocoa, up 40% year-over-year to $10,000 per metric ton from West African shortages, hit our chocolate products, but our hedging—covering 70% of 2024 needs at $7,200 per ton—offset 60% of the pressure, saving $45 million in COGS.

Pricing actions added 100 basis points via 4-6% increases on 65% of the portfolio, with solid uptake in premium lines. PlantPower shakes took a 5.5% hike, holding volumes steady as health-focused consumers traded up, with elasticity at -2.5 versus the industry's -3.0 per IRI.

Product mix shift drove 80 basis points, as premium and plant-based items hit 28% of sales, up from 22%. Organic snack bars and low-sugar NutriSpark beverages grew 18% year-over-year at over 55% margins, compared to 38% for traditional sodas—echoing Nestlé's premium plays.

Operational efficiencies contributed 50 basis points: bottling yields rose 2.5% with AI fillers, saving $28 million; lighter PET bottles cut packaging by 7%; freight eased 5% post-surcharges.

Historically, margins climbed from 42.1% in Q3 2022 through 2023's 44.6% trough as 2022's 25% commodity surges—from Ukraine and canal issues—unwound. We see another 100-150 basis points expansion in FY24, Q4 at 47.5%, barring avian flu or El Niño risks capped at 50 basis points downside.

Regionally: North America (55% revenue) at 49.2%, plus 300 basis points on retail pricing and RTD coffee growth; EMEA (25%) at 43.5%, plus 150 basis points despite energy inflation, aided by gas hedges; APAC/LatAm (20%) at 47.8%, plus 250 basis points on volume in Indonesia tea and Brazil juices.

Initiatives include SAP S/4HANA for 95% accurate COGS forecasting, blockchain supplier portals for $60 million savings, regenerative farming for 10% fertilizer cuts, portfolio optimization divesting low-margin sodas, a Brazilian sugar mill acquisition, and expanded hedging to 65%.

Next, volume and price/mix analysis underpinned our 5.2% net revenue growth to $12.4 billion, with organic up 4.8%—12 straight quarters positive. This beat peers like PepsiCo's 1-2%, driven by 1.2% volume and 3.6% price/mix across NutriSpark, BevPure, CrunchBar, and PlantPower.

Volumes held resilient at +1.2%, up 200 basis points from Q2, despite at-home slowdowns. Beverages (61% revenue, +1.5%) led with CSDs up 2.1% on zero-sugar NutriSpark gaining 1.2 share points per IRI; functional BevPure+ electrolytes +4.8% versus category decline; waters flat but ahead of Coke. Snacks (29%, +0.8%): CrunchBar savory +1.5% on low-sodium; sweets -0.5% lapping comps. Nutrition (10%, +0.4%): PlantPower +3.2% via e-com.

By region: North America (51%, +1.8%) on convenience velocity; EMEA (21%, flat) balanced by emerging markets; APAC (15%, +2.4%) on localized NutriSpark; LatAm (10%, -0.5%) weather-hit but snacks steady. Enablers: $250 million shopper marketing, 97% availability from Memphis facility.

Price/mix +3.6%: ASP +2.9%, mix +0.7%. Pricing 2-4% on 70% portfolio with 95% acceptance; premium zero-sugar at 28% of bev sales, plant-based snacks 12%. North America +4.2%, EMEA +3.1%, others strong.

Outlook: 3-5% organic FY24, +1-2% volume on innovations like NutriSpark Immunity; $400 million R&D; e-com 18%; hedging 80%.

Turning to input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions—these pressured COGS by 220 basis points sequentially, mirroring Hershey's cocoa, Kellogg's wheat issues. Inflation averaged 12% year-over-year, up from Q2's 9%: wheat +18% from Ukraine cuts; palm oil +22% on El Niño; cocoa +42%; dairy +14%; packaging +16%. North America labor/freight +25%; Europe energy 3x; APAC floods; LatAm stable.

Disruptions: $28 million charges; Red Sea added 10-14 days, freight +35%; delays in cocoa/dairy; turns 8.2x, safety stock +15 days tying $150 million capital.

Mitigations: 9% pricing rounds, 65% pass-through, ASP +7.2%; hedging 70% wheat/oil; supplier diversification to 12% Ukrainian wheat; Midwest farm for 10% grain savings; SAP IBP 92% accuracy, 8% waste cut; SKU prune 12%; contracts 55%.

Inflation to 7-9% Q4; EBITDA 18.4%, down 80 basis points; $45 million productivity.

Organic revenue growth hit 7.2%, sixth straight quarter beating 5-6% guide; YTD 6.8%, on track for 6-7% FY. Pricing +3.8 points vs. 12-15% COGS; volume +2.5; mix +0.9 premium.

North America (45%, 5.1%): snacks +1.3 points share; Europe (25%, 8.9%): yogurt/RTD coffee +3.1 volumes; APAC (20%, 12.3%): India/SEA +6.2; LatAm (8%, 4.5%) pricing +6.2.

Strategy: Flavor Forward 2025, $200 million functional R&D; trade efficiency; raised FY to 6.5-7.5%.

On EPS guidance: FY24 $4.85-$5.05, +12-16% over $4.32; constant currency 14-18%. Organic revenue 4-6%, Q4 5-7%. Beverages mid-single, snacks low-double, dairy/plant 6-8%; NA 5-7%, EMEA flat-2%, APAC/LatAm 7-9%.

Margins: gross +150-200bps to 38.5-39%; commodities favorable 2-3%, hedging 80%; $250 million FreshFlow savings; op income +10-13%, 17.5-18% margin; SG&A -50bps. Interest $180 million, tax 23.5%, shares 420 million.

HealthForward: 20% innovation sugar-reduced; DTC 25%; $100 million packaging.

Risks: inflation, recession, FX.

Finally, market share trends: U.S. F&B beverages +3.2%; FreshFizz CSD 14.2%, +80bps YoY on FizzFit zero-sugar 42% mix, 92% ACV. VitaSurge energy 9.6%, +220bps top-5, SurgeFlow +45%. APAC FreshFizz tea 4.7% China; EU dip offset stevia; LatAm +1.8 Brazil. HydraBars snacks 3.1%, +90bps.

Trends: premium 38%; e-com +22%; sustainability. FY24 +100-150bps; $220 million CapEx.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from Mike Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

Mike Chen (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of input cost inflation on your business?

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thanks, Mike. As Jordan detailed, inflation averaged 12% across our basket, with spikes in wheat, oils, cocoa, and dairy pressuring COGS. But our aggressive pricing—totaling 9% with strong pass-through—hedging covering 70% of key needs, supplier shifts, and farm integration limited the hit. We're seeing moderation ahead, positioning us to expand margins further.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Lisa Wong (JPMorgan):
What are your plans for PlantPower protein shakes and what is the expected revenue impact?

Taylor Kim (Chief Growth Officer):
Great question, Lisa. PlantPower is central to our premiumization, with 5.5% pricing holding volumes flat amid trade-up from millennials. We've ramped e-com to 15% of sales, reformulated for better-for-you appeal, and plan Q4 launches tying into functional trends—expecting 15-20% revenue lift in nutrition, contributing 40 basis points to mix.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Ruiz with Barclays. Please proceed.

David Ruiz (Barclays):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Chris Patel (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
David, disruptions like Red Sea routes and port congestion added costs and delays, slowing turns to 8.2x. We've built safety stock smartly, diversified suppliers—cutting Ukraine reliance—added co-packers like Memphis, and deployed SAP IBP for 92% forecast accuracy. Freight should ease 15-20% in Q4, with vertical integration securing inputs.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Emily Park with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Emily Park (Morgan Stanley):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Jordan Lee (CFO):
Emily, we're reaffirming FY24 guidance with confidence: 4-6% organic sales, accelerating Q4; gross margins expanding 150-200 basis points on productivity and hedging; EPS $4.85-$5.05. Key assumptions hold—modest inflation, volume stabilization, share gains—and upside from innovations and channel shifts. We're executing sharply.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in NutriBev Inc. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
